why_angle: The cited keyboard-tablet roundup gives only its own battery hours, which put the S10 FE last, and the makers' brightness claims, and it leaves out the Lenovo Idea Tab Pro. No cited page has Notebookcheck's lab figures, which reverse that battery order (S10 FE 14 h 47 min vs S11 11 h 14 min) and show the Idea Tab Pro at 409 cd/m². This page has those measurements for every candidate, plus Samsung US totals for each tablet with its own keyboard and which of those keyboards have a trackpad.

page.desc: Samsung Galaxy Tab S10 FE, S10 FE+, Tab S11 and S11 Ultra compared with Notebookcheck's battery and brightness tests, plus the cost with Samsung's own keyboard.
page.answer: Short answer. The best-value Android tablet with keyboard in 2026 is the Samsung Galaxy Tab S10 FE with Samsung's trackpad Book Cover Keyboard, sold separately. Notebookcheck measured 14 h 47 min of Wi-Fi browsing, against 11 h 14 min for the Galaxy Tab S11, which has no trackpad keyboard.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Galaxy Tab S10 FE with its trackpad keyboard: $549.99 + $199.99 = $749.98 at Samsung US on 2026-11-10. The keyboard adds 36% to the tablet's price ($199.99 ÷ $549.99).
  • Galaxy Tab S11 with its only Samsung keyboard: $999.99 + $144.99 = $1,144.98, which is $395.00 more than the S10 FE kit, and the S11 kit has no trackpad. Samsung's buy page lists the S11 from $999.99 without naming the storage size.
  • Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra: $1,299.99 + $209.99 = $1,509.98 with the Slim keyboard (no trackpad), or $1,299.99 + $399.99 = $1,699.98 with the trackpad Pro Keyboard.
  • Battery: 14 h 47 min − 11 h 14 min = 3 h 33 min more Wi-Fi browsing for the S10 FE than the S11. The S10 FE+ adds another 18 h 56 min − 14 h 47 min = 4 h 09 min.
  • Carry weight: S10 FE 497 g + trackpad keyboard 423 g = 920 g, about 2.03 lb.

Measured battery life and brightness: what a keyboard workload gets

Once a tablet sits in a keyboard cover, it spends hours with the screen on, browsing and editing documents. Notebookcheck runs the same Wi-Fi browsing script and measures maximum brightness with a colorimeter on every tablet it tests, so these figures compare directly:

TabletWi-Fi browsingMax brightnessBattery
Galaxy Tab S10 FE+18 h 56 min789 cd/m²10,090 mAh
Galaxy Tab S10 FE14 h 47 min667 cd/m²8,000 mAh
Lenovo Idea Tab Pro Gen 2 (13.0-inch)14 h 11 min618 cd/m²n/a
Lenovo Idea Tab Pro (12.7-inch)13 h 18 min409 cd/m²10,200 mAh
Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra (5G)13 h 9 min1,017 cd/m²11,600 mAh
Galaxy Tab S1111 h 14 min955 cd/m²8,400 mAh

The two FE models have the smallest processors and the largest batteries for their size, and they ran longest. The S11 and S11 Ultra have the brightest screens but ran shorter. MyNextTablet's own battery test put the S10 FE at 8.5 h and the S11 at 12.75 h, the opposite order. Its test script differs from Notebookcheck's, so compare each lab's figures only with that lab's other results.

The 12.7-inch Lenovo Idea Tab Pro is the dim one: 409 ÷ 667 = 61% of the S10 FE's measured brightness. It has two strengths: Notebookcheck confirms its USB-C port outputs DisplayPort video, and its keyboard dock attaches by pogo pins. The Idea Tab Pro Gen 2 fixes the brightness at 618 cd/m².

Every Samsung keyboard here attaches by pogo pins, so there is no Bluetooth pairing or keyboard battery to charge. Samsung US now also titles the S11 Ultra keyboards for a Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra, so check that newer model before paying Ultra prices.

Not recommended

Galaxy Tab S11 as a laptop replacement. Samsung sells only the Book Cover Keyboard Slim for it, with no trackpad option, so you need a separate mouse to use DeX like a laptop. It also had the shortest Wi-Fi runtime Notebookcheck measured here (11 h 14 min), and with its keyboard it costs $1,144.98. As a light tablet for typing only it works well. For keyboard-first use, the S10 FE kit costs $395.00 less, has a trackpad and runs 3 h 33 min longer.
